summary.outcome: No reviewed official-vendor HLS family had enough public source-specific evidence to close third-party native playback. Catalogue permission statuses remain unchanged.

prototype_policy: Technically public HLS remains sufficient for native client-side playback unless recorded rights evidence requires link-out; pending direct streams stay visibly permission-pending.

families.reason: Ontario public terms support reasonable, fair, non-commercial use of excerpts with credit and media guidance expects accredited media to use the Assembly broadcast feed, but the public evidence still does not clearly authorize full live-stream relay by an independent public app.
The official webcast page exposes live and downloadable archive video, but no explicit reuse terms were found for full third-party live playback.
Sansad TV is an official parliamentary channel, but no direct Sansad TV reuse terms were found; Digital Sansad policy language points to permission for reproduction beyond source acknowledgement.

Knesset broadcast law/guidance appears to support proceedings use with visible credit, but the permanent channel also carries non-proceeding programming that may need authorization and the catalogue cannot yet distinguish those states.
Assembly ownership rules establish institutional source ownership and restrict editing/commercialization, but do not clearly authorize third-party native playback of the live ARTV stream.

Portal terms support limited republication of parts of site content with attribution and no alteration, but do not clearly authorize full third-party live-stream playback of the parliamentary TV channel.
The official television page confirms the source surface, but no source-specific terms were found that close third-party native playback.
The endpoint remained permission-pending because the prior validation environment could not reach it and no source-specific third-party native playback terms were found.
The two official live-room streams remain pending because no source-specific terms were found for third-party native playback.
The official MediaPortal confirms the live/video surface, but no source-specific third-party native playback terms were found.
The official page labels the embedded live surface as Canal Parlamento, but the page footer reserves rights and no explicit third-party native playback terms were found.
